chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 1F Entry Chamber
chunks.x: Crystal Peak – 1F Entry Chamber | The entryway. The first chamber you enter is a small one – walk north and you’ll see a Healing Chansey. | The Healing Chansey. Walk east from there and you’ll see some rocks to be smashed and boulders to be pushed., It’s not a puzzle really, just make sure the way through is unblocked. | The ladder down. Once you force your way past that obstacle, you’ll see a ladder down to a lower floor.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – B1F Rune Chamber
chunks.x: Crystal Peak – B1F Rune Chamber | Another small chamber. When you arrive, you’ll see a pond to the east along a passageway. Surf across it until you see dry land. | A fork in the road. The north way leads to a room with a Hiker and three strange tablets – you’ll need to ignore them for now, since they can only be interacted with in the post-game., Take the east way instead. | Another ladder. You’ll see a ladder leading up to a different chamber on 1F.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 1F Main Chamber
chunks.x: Crystal Peak – 1F Main Chamber | The main chamber. This is a fairly large chamber, though a lot of it is blocked off., Climb down the blue crystals on the wall to get to the cavern floor. | Medium Laurel. Go west here, passing by Medium Laurel, until you see a sloping ledge to the west. | The yellow crystal handholds. Climb up the yellow crystals and you’ll be on an upper ledge. Follow the ledge south.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 1F Main Chamber
chunks.x: Cyclist Lucina will run into you here. You may encounter Cyclist Lucina on the way. Keep going until you reach a junction as seen below. | The junction. The path to the left leads to a tunnel entrance that is a dead end right now, so the only path forward is to climb down the yellow crystals. | The first Light of Ruin grunts. Squeeze your way through the crystals on the path ahead and you’ll run right into the first Light of Ruin Grunts in the cave.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 1F Main Chamber
chunks.x: The tunnel to the outside. After you and your Rival beat them, you’ll see a tunnel in the wall that leads to Crystal Peak’s exterior.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior
chunks.x: Crystal Peak – Exterior | Crystal Peak Exterior map. Final Confrontation. Crystal Peak Exterior Slopes to 1F Main Chamber, Crystal Peak Exterior Summit to 5F Antechamber

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior
chunks.x: Items: Nugget, X Defense, Full Restore (hidden), Zygarde Cell, Escape Rope (hidden), Green Shard (hidden) | Items: Zygarde Cell | Wild Pokémon (Exterior): Drifblim (Ghost/Flying) Lv50–54 85%, Rufflet (Normal/Flying) Lv50–54 5%, Vullaby (Dark/Flying) Lv50–54 5%, Absol (Dark/Flying) Lv50–54 5%

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior
chunks.x: Exterior Slopes | Outside on the rocky slopes. There aren’t any trainers out here, but there are a few wild Pokémon that can still reach you, so head west up the blue crystals to try and find another way inside the mountain., Once you’ve climbed them, there’s a longer set of orange crystals you’ll need to make your way up. | The path branches. Once you arrive on a ledge, take the yellow crystals north. | Another crystal choice. Then climb up the blue crystals on the right side.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior
chunks.x: The upper ledges of the path. Keep going until you have to climb a yellow set of crystals, and then an orange set., You’ll see the entrance into upper Crystal Peak from there. | The top of the mountain awaits. Head inside the cave and you’ll find yourself on 2F.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Middle Floors
chunks.x: Crystal Peak – Middle Floors | Crystal Peak 2F and 3F maps. Light of Ruin Grunt Pair B, Light of Ruin Grunt Pair C, Pokémon Storage Porygon, Tao Dragon Double Battle. 2F Middle Chamber to Crystal Peak Exterior Slopes, 2F Middle Chamber to 3F Dragon Chamber, 3F Dragon Chamber to 4F Jail Chamber | Trainer Light of Ruin Grunt Pair B: Carbink (Rock/Fairy) Lv53, Clefable (Ghost/Flying) Lv54, Sylveon (Fairy) Lv54, Shiinotic (Grass/Fairy) Lv54

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Middle Floors
chunks.x: Trainer Light of Ruin Grunt Pair C: Aromatisse (Fairy) Lv54, Slurpuff (Fairy) Lv54, Alolan Ninetales (Ice/Fairy) Lv55, Ribombee (Bug/Fairy) Lv54 | Crystal Peak – 2F Middle Chamber | The beginning of 2F. A lot of this floor is currently inaccessible, so the way through is fairly simple to navigate. | The next pair of grunts. You’ll see two Light of Ruin grunts guarding a passage west – take them on and head through it when you’re done.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 2F Middle Chamber
chunks.x: The next ladder. Follow the passage along, up a couple of crystal rock climb walls, until you see the ladder for the next floor. | Crystal Peak – 3F Dragon Chamber | The third floor. This floor is another linear one, with an optional path that you’ll need to ignore., Surf across the pond to the north and follow the winding passage until you see more Grunts. | The third set of grunts. Apparently Jax has been through here and already beaten them – but they’re still up to be defeated by you.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 3F Dragon Chamber
chunks.x: The Pokemon Storage Porygon. At the very end of the winding passage you’ll see a Porygon to switch out your Pokémon with, and the unmistakable signs of an upcoming boss room. | Dragon Showdown | Zekrom and Reshiram. The Light of Ruin want to delay you as long as possible, so Hoopa has summoned the Legendary Pokémon Zekrom and Reshiram to face you in a Double Battle with your Rival!, The Dragons scale to your level, so it can be an extremely tough fight. | If you’ve got that Alolan Ninetales with the Icium-Z, it can be used to take out Zekrom immediately to even things up. | Trainer Tao Dragons Double Battle: Reshiram (Dragon/Fire (level scaled)) Lv?, Zekrom (Dragon/Electric (level scaled)) Lv?

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Dragon Showdown
chunks.x: Ivory shows up to delay you as well. After you defeat the dragons, it’s not over., Ivory comes down to battle you herself, though not before having to knock out her own son. | Trainer Light of Ruin Admin Ivory: Mismagius (Ghost) Lv57, Incineroar (Fire/Dark) Lv58, Mandibuzz (Dark/Flying) Lv57, Alakazam (Mega) (Psychic) Lv58 | Ivory leaves you to continue on. After beating her, Ivory retreats and your Rival recovers, ready to press on to the top of the mountain.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Dragon Showdown
chunks.x: The ladder up. When the cutscene is over, take the ladder to 4F. | Crystal Peak – Upper Floors | Crystal Peak 4F and 5F maps. Light of Ruin Grunt Pair D, Marlon and Melony, Light of Grunt Line of Sight Puzzle, Healing Chansey and Pokémon Storage Porygon. 4F Jail Chamber to 3F Dragon Chamber, 4F Jail Chamber to 5F Antechamber, 5F Antechamber to Crystal Peak Exterior Summit

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Upper Floors
chunks.x: Items: PP Up | Trainer Light of Ruin Grunt Pair D: Mimikyu (Ghost/Fairy) Lv55, Togekiss (Fairy/Flying) Lv55, Gardevoir (Psychic/Fairy) Lv56 | Crystal Peak – 4F Jail Chamber | Arriving on 4F. There is a constant sandstorm raging here that will damage any battling Pokémon that isn’t Rock-, Steel-, or Ground-type. | Beating the jailers. Cross the pond east and you’ll run into a final pair of Grunts. They’re guarding some familiar prisoners.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 4F Jail Chamber
chunks.x: A small boulder puzzle. But there’s a small boulder puzzle blocking your way forward:, Step 1: Push the middle boulder north once. | Step 2: Use Rock Smash on the east rock., Step 3: Push the right boulder east to the wall. | After the second move. Step 4: Push the upper boulder west to the wall. | After the third move. Then once that’s done, the path will be clear.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 4F Jail Chamber
chunks.x: Marlon tries to break out from the wrong side. Marlon and Melony are trapped behind another boulder, but Marlon’s Krookodile can’t push it from that side. Your Rival helps them out. | The Prison Bottle acquired. You’ll get the Prison Bottle to hopefully use on Hoopa if given the opportunity., Marlon warns you that the guard ahead has some sort of hypnotizing power, so you’ll need to find some way past him without being seen. | Further along the passage. Walk east and you’ll see a pond to surf across.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 4F Jail Chamber
chunks.x: The guard cannot be allowed to see you. Once you’re on the other side, smash all of the rocks – making sure not to step into the Grunt’s line of sight – and then push the boulder east so it’s just southwest of him (see the screenshot below). | One more push. Then push the boulder north and that will block you from view. | The ladder to 5F. Climb up the ladder and you’ll be on the top floor.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – 5F Antechamber
chunks.x: Crystal Peak – 5F Antechamber | More signs of an upcoming boss battle. A Healing Chansey and Pokémon Storage Porygon confirm that this is the beginning of the end, so heal and swap out Pokémon as necessary. | The way to the summit. When you’re ready, take the opening outside to the summit of Crystal Peak. | Crystal Peak – Exterior Summit | Crystal Peak’s highest height. When you’re outside, head up the first set of stairs. You’ll be stopped by Jax and Arthur, who are hiding and want to use a bit of stealth.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior Summit
chunks.x: Jax and Arthur. You’ll get told to wait until Aklove makes an appearance, and then a move can be made. | Aklove and Ivory prepare to fire the Ultimate Weapon. The Ultimate Weapon is here, a massive crystal structure that used to be in Kalos., Before Aklove can fire it however, Jax makes his move and everyone rushes in to do battle. | Hoopa confronts you. Aklove sends Hoopa to deal with you, and Hoopa brings along Mega Rayquaza to make things a little difficult., Not to worry though – that Icium-Z trick works as well on Rayquaza as it did on Zekrom. | Trainer Hoopa and Rayquaza Double Battle: Hoopa Unbound (Psychic/Dark (level scaled)) Lv?, Rayquaza ((Mega) Dragon/Flying (level scaled)) Lv?

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior Summit
chunks.x: Hoopa is back to its old self. Hoopa freaks out at being defeated and starts releasing portals left and right – these may cause a bit of an issue later!, However, you reach for the Prison Bottle just in time and manage to seal it back to its Confined Forme. | The Hoopa joins you | Getting Hoopa | Since you’re Aros’ child, the Hoopa is yours by rights apparently, and it joins your team or gets sent to a Box if it’s full., You can use the Prison Bottle on it to switch between Confined and Unbound Formes. | Reward Pokémon: Hoopa Confined (Psychic/Ghost) Lv60

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior Summit
chunks.x: One thing left to do. With no time to spare, you’ll need to shut down the Ultimate Weapon for good. | Facing Aklove | Aklove is determined to destroy Borrius. Try and make for the Ultimate Weapon’s controls, and Aklove will stop you. It’s time to take him down. | Light of Ruin Leader Double Battle | Trainer Aklove: Klefki (Steel/Fairy) Lv56, Primarina (Water/Fairy) Lv57, Raichu (Electric) Lv57, Gardevoir (Psychic/Fairy) Lv58, Roserade (Grass/Poison) Lv57. Prize ₽24,400

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior Summit
chunks.x: Aklove does not take defeat well. Aklove takes his loss just as well as Hoopa did, and starts freaking out. He pushes past you to activate the Ultimate Weapon anyway, and it hits Dresco Town!, However, before anyone can react, someone unexpected arrives. | Zeph saved the day. Unbeknownst to Aklove, Zeph snuck in to change the Ultimate Weapon’s controls while he wasn’t looking, and set the machine to ‘create’ instead of ‘destroy’., The beam was harmless to Dresco Town, and there’s no more Shadow Warriors so the weapon has no more energy. | The Light of Ruin are no more. | Arthur arrives with the cavalry. Aklove is handed in to Arthur and the Pokémon Rangers, and so is Zeph – but Marlon is left alone., You might think it’s over, but it isn’t – there’s one last battle to fight, and it’s a Double Battle.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior Summit
chunks.x: Your Rival wants to fight beside you against his father. Marlon is your final opponent on Crystal Peak, to prove to your Rival that you can take him down together. | Trainer Marlon: Krookodile (Ground/Dark) Lv58, Cacturne (Grass/Dark) Lv56, Sharpedo ((Mega) Water/Dark) Lv57, Dusknoir (Ghost) Lv57, Roserade (Grass/Poison) Lv57. Prize ₽14,880 | After You Win | The battle is over. With everyone at Crystal Peak taken care of, it’s time to move on to the final challenge of the main story of Pokémon Unbound – the Pokémon League.

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Crystal Peak – Exterior Summit
chunks.x: The last gym awaits. Redwood Gym is the final one you need a Badge from, and you can get there by heading east from Magnolia Town., However, before you do, there’s a very special item worth collecting. | Obtaining the Master Ball | The house of the two elders in Epidimy Town. Remember how in Epidimy Town there’s a couple of old people keeping something for the Guardian of Borrius? | You’re the Guardian now. Well, possession of Hoopa is what qualifies someone for that title, and now that is you., The precious item they’ve been keeping for Aros’ successor is the Master Ball. Use it wisely!

chunks.t: Part 35: Crystal Peak – Obtaining the Master Ball
chunks.x: Your prize – the Master Ball. Then once you’re ready to go, Fly back to Magnolia Town and head east – it’s time to get that final badge. | Heading to Redwood Town

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Magnolia Fields map. HiHorsepower Trainer, Rancher Carter, Safari Zone Mission, Fisherman Jasper, Rancher Molly, Jogger Beck, Savanna Vivillon, Swimmer Darcie, Bug Catcher Brent. Magnolia Town, Redwood Village

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Items: Heart Scale (hidden), Net Ball, Zinc, Zygarde Cell, Max Repel (hidden), Elixir (hidden) | Items: Max Potion, Zygarde Cell, Rare Candy (hidden), TM22 Solar Beam, X Sp. Def

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Wild Pokémon [Long Grass]: Tranquill (Normal/Flying Day and Night), Furfrou (Normal Day and Night) Lv48–53 20%, Mudsdale (Ground Day and Night) Lv48–53 25%, Gogoat (Grass Day and Night) Lv48–53 10%, Miltank (Normal Day and Night) Lv48–53 9%, Tauros (Normal Day and Night) Lv48–53 1%, Noctowl (Normal/Flying Night) Lv48–53 Day 0% / Night X% | Wild Pokémon [Surfing]: Frillish (Water/Ghost) Lv45–50 60%, Pelipper (Water/Flying) Lv45–40 30%, Jellicent (Water/Ghost) Lv48–50 10% | Wild Pokémon [Fishing]: Magikarp (Water (Old Rod)) Lv10–15 100%, Gyarados (Water/Flying (Good Rod)) Lv20–50, Wailmer (Water (Good Rod)) Lv20–25 40%, Wailord (Water (Super Rod)) Lv45–50 45%, Gyarados (Water/Flying (Super Rod)) Lv20–50, Qwilfish (Water/Poison (Super Rod)) Lv45–50 15%

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Trainer Rancher Carter: Furfrou (Normal) Lv55, Mudsdale (Ground) Lv56, Tauros (Normal) Lv57. Prize ₽2,600 | Trainer Fisherman Jasper: Qwilfish (Water/Poison) Lv55, Qwilfish (Water/Poison) Lv57. Prize ₽2,080 | Trainer Rancher Molly: Furfrou (Normal) Lv55, Gogoat (Grass) Lv56, Miltank (Normal) Lv57. Prize ₽304 | Trainer Jogger Beck: Unfezant (Normal/Flying) Lv57, Unfezant (Normal/Flying) Lv56. Prize ₽2,016 | Trainer Swimmer Darcie: Jellicent (Water/Ghost) Lv57. Prize ₽1,512

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Trainer Bug Catcher Brent: Pineco (Bug) Lv56, Scyther (Bug/Flying) Lv57. Prize ₽768 | This Rancher will train a move. The final Badge in the Pokémon League is in Redwood Village, and the only way to get there is to cross through Magnolia Fields., The first person you see is a move trainer who will teach a Pokémon HiHorsepower for 3 Yellow Shards. | A New Mission | Follow the path south and through the trees. The road may end here, but the path doesn’t., Go south and you’ll be led through a long path through some trees and long grass.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Rancher Carter. Rancher Carter will probably run into you somewhere along here., You’ll eventually come to a fork in the forest path. | East to the coast, north leads further into woodland. For now, go north and follow the trees along until you see a Trainer Tips sign and another choice to make. | West and north paths through more trees. Take the west path through the trees and you’ll see a man with orange hair who has a mission for you.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: The Safari Zone mission. In order to complete the mission, you’ll need to catch 25 Pokémon in one single session of the Safari Zone – considering you only have 30 Balls total, it’s a pretty tall order, even on Easy difficulty., If you manage it though, you’ll get 30 Beast Balls – useful for catching Ultra Beasts in the endgame. | Finding a Vivillon | Fisherman Jasper and the southern water crossing. Go all the way back to the first fork in the woods, near Rancher Carter, and head east through the long grass to the shoreline and Fisherman Jasper. | The middle part of the Fields is barren. Surf east in this lower part of the water channel and you’ll see a barren patch of land., Apparently the Guardian Pokémon of this route is gone, and the area is slowly dying.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Rancher Molly. Rancher Molly takes her anger about this out on you, but once you’ve defeated her you can move to the east side and surf across to the other shore. | Jogger Beck. Jogger Beck is waiting for you on the other side., After that, head southeast and you’ll see a small passage to a southern clearing. | The Savanna Vivillon. One of the 19 Vivillon the collector in Magnolia Town told you about here – you can defeat it or try and catch it, but the difficulty in catching is turned way up for these so it may take a few tries., That’s it for this section of the Fields – so you can go all the way back to the Trainer Tips sign on the west bank and head north to continue.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Continuing Forward | The way to the other water passage. Redwood Village is on the eastern back but you’ll need to take the northern water passage to get there. Cut a small tree down and walk northeast and you’ll eventually see the shore. | The shore. Surf east through the rocks. You’ll probably encounter Swimmer Darcie on the way. | Swimmer Darcie. After you pass Darcie, it’s a long surf until you get to the northeast shore.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: A little bit of the decay is here too. Bug Catcher Brent is here to greet you with a battle – once done, continue east and you’ll make it to the Redwood Village entrance. | Redwood Village entrance. Go east into the trees and you’ll find yourself in a small, dark, wooded area – welcome to Redwood. | Items: Net Ball, Max Repel, Heart Scale, Zinc, Max Potion, Rare Candy, X Sp. Def, Reveal Glass, Beast Ball x30, TM22 Solar Beam, Trainer Tips sign #40, Zygarde Cell #95, Zygarde Cell #96, Portal #25, Blacephalon, Vivillon pattern Savanna, Max Raid Den #18

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Magnolia Fields
chunks.x: Special Encounters (Miraheze wiki): Vivillon (Savanna form) Lv50, Tornadus (Incarnate form) Lv77, Thundurus (Incarnate form) Lv77, Landorus (Incarnate form) Lv70 | Redwood Village | Redwood Village map. Pokémon Center, Poke Mart, Babysitting House, Breeder House, Cleanse Tag Medium, Magikarp Mission House, Redwood Gym. Magnolia Fields, Redwood Forest | Items: Tanga Berry, Zygarde Cell, TM102 Dazzle Gleam

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Village
chunks.x: Wild Pokémon [Headbutt]: Aipom (Normal) Lv10–30 30%, Pineco (Bug) Lv10–30 60%, Scyther (Bug/Flying) Lv50 4%, Pinsir (Bug) Lv50 1%, Heracross (Bug/Fighting) Lv50 5% | The village in the woods. Redwood Village is pretty small, but it does have the final Gym in the League. So it’s worth looking around a little while you’re here., If you have a Pokémon that knows Headbutt, you can use it on the trees here to encounter a variety of wild Pokémon. | Tip: There’s no Headbutt TM in the game, but various Pokémon you may have encountered such as Litleo and Cubone learn the move through leveling. | The woman in the Pokemon Center wants to see something. When you head into the Pokémon Center, go up to the woman on the west wall and she’ll want to see a Pokémon holding Charcoal., If you go and pick Tepig up from the house on Route 5 giving away Unova starters, it will be holding a Charcoal. Show that to her and she’ll give you a Luck Incense.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Village
chunks.x: The final trade. If you’re doing the trading mission, the final trade in the main game of Pokémon Unbound is here on the east side of the Pokémon Center., Balogna wants a Zweilous in exchange for a Lampent. | Pokémon Trade: Lampent (Ghost/Fire), Zweilous (Dark/Dragon found in Crystal Peak) | The Pokémon Center and the Poke Mart, at the crossroads in town. When you’re finished healing and shopping, head east along the main road.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Village
chunks.x: Babysitting for Quick Cash | This household needs a favor. Go inside the house in the northeast corner of the village, where you’ll get an unusual request – but only during 7am-7pm. | Babysitting?. Apparently your services as a babysitter are required, just for a minute or two., Say yes, and you’ll have to walk around Redwood Village for a while with a baby in tow! | Tip: If you turn and speak to the baby it should give you a Rare Candy. | Follower acquired. Take the baby around for a spin for a little while, maybe just a couple minutes. Then you can return to the house.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Village
chunks.x: The reward. When you return the baby you’ll get a very respectable P10,000., Not bad! | The western house. Next, head to the house south of the Pokémon Center, up against the west edge of the village. | The Breeders House | The Breeder couple. There’s a couple of Breeders inside – the woman will speed up all Eggs in your party for a fee that increases every time you use it.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Village
chunks.x: Unwanted eggs are sold here. If there are any Eggs you don’t want, you can sell them off to the male Breeder for P2000 each. | Other Items To Get | The old woman thinks we are a ghost. Speak to the old woman wandering around on the south end of town and you’ll get a Cleanse Tag. | The Fishing House. The house in the southeast corner has a member of the Hip Waders fisherman’s club in it, and he offers a mission to fellow members.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Village
chunks.x: Catch Magikarp. You just have to catch all the Magikarp you can, which is easy with an Old Rod., If you manage to fill up a Box with them, you’ll get a Shiny Magikarp for your trouble. | Reward Pokémon: Magikarp ((Shiny) Water) | With all that done in the village, it’s time to go to the last Gym in the Pokémon League and earn that Badge. | Redwood Gym

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Village
chunks.x: Items: Luck Incense, Fresh Water, Bug Gem, TM49 Leech Fang, Cleanse Tag, TM102 Dazzling Gleam, Tanga Berry, Zygarde Cell #97 | Special Encounters (Miraheze wiki): Celebi (Special) Lv65 | Redwood Gym – Time Badge | This is a strange Gym. The Redwood Gym is a Bug-type Gym, which should be a pushover for Fire, Flying- and Rock-types, right? Well, yes., But that’s not the only mechanic at work in this Gym. | The gimmick here is that to earn the Time Badge, you’ll have to fight Pokémon that, instead of fainting, merely regress to their pre-evolution form, until they run out of those forms., So most Pokémon here have two or three phases., This also applies to your Pokémon too – and they’ll go back to normal at the end of each battle – but be aware that Pokémon can forget moves and get weaker as they devolve.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Gym – Time Badge
chunks.x: Gym Trainers | Trainer Ace Trainer Daisy: Accelgor (Bug devolves to Shelmet Bug (Lv.58)) Lv58, Scolipede (Bug/Poison devolves to Whirlipede Bug/Poison (Lv.58) devolves to Venipede Bug/Poison (Lv.58)) Lv58. Prize ₽252 | Trainer Ninja Bug Fuller: Ariados (Bug/Poison devolves to Spinarak Bug/Poison (Lv.57)) Lv57. Prize ₽1,008 | Trainer Expert Tizzy: Yanmega (Bug/Flying devolves to Yanma Bug/Flying (Lv.58)) Lv58, Vikavolt (Bug/Electric devolves to Charjabug Bug/Electric (Lv.58) devolves to Grubbin Bug (Lv.58)) Lv58. Prize ₽2,520 | Trainer Bug Catcher Curtis: Beedrill (Bug/Poison devolves to Kakuna Bug/Poison (Lv.58) devolves to Weedle Bug/Poison (Lv.58)) Lv58. Prize ₽4,080

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Gym – Time Badge
chunks.x: The Gym Puzzle | There are four trainers you need to beat before facing Benjamin, the Gym Leader. And each trainer is in their own room., There’s also a button in a rock in each room. | There’s no puzzle, just four rooms. After beating all four trainers in their rooms, you’ll have to hit the buttons in a particular order – only then will the final room open., This order is hinted at by the trainers, but it can actually be figured out two ways: | The themes of the rooms each trainer is in – each represent a major story dungeon. You have to go backwards through the story to get the order, so that would be Crystal Peak – Thundercap Mountain – Cinder Volcano – Icicle Cave., Or, like Benjamin Button – you simply push them in reverse order of the trainers’ ages: elderly Expert Tizzy – adult Ace Trainer Daisy – teenager Bug Catcher Curtis – child Ninja Boy Fuller. | Here is the correct button order for the gym puzzle.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Gym – Time Badge
chunks.x: Items: Expert Tizzy’s Room (Crystal Peak), Ace Trainer Daisy’s Room (Thundercap Mountain), Bug Catcher Curtis’ Room (Cinder Volcano), Ninja Boy Fuller’s Room (Icicle Cave) | The way is open. Once you’ve pushed the buttons in the correct order, you’re ready to face the final Gym Leader in Borrius.

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Gym – Time Badge
chunks.x: Redwood Gym Leader – Benjamin | Benjamin is old. Benjamin puts up a tough fight, even with Bug Pokémon – all of his bugs are interesting double types, and Drapion isn’t even technically Bug-type, though it evolves from one. | Tip: The table below is only for Benjamin on Vanilla mode. If you are playing on a higher difficulty level then visit our Redwood Village Gym page here to see his team comps at other difficulties. | Trainer Gym Leader Benjamin: Araquanid (Water/Bug devolves to Dewpider Water/Bug (Lv.59)) Lv59, Scizor ((Mega) Bug/Steel devolves to Scyther Bug/Flying (Lv.60)) Lv60, Drapion (Poison/Dark devolves to Skorupi Poison/Bug (Lv.61)) Lv61, Butterfree (Bug/Flying devolves to Metapod Bug (Lv.60) devolves to Caterpie Bug (Lv.60)) Lv60. Prize ₽9,920

chunks.t: Part 36: Magnolia Fields, Redwood Village & Redwood Gym – Redwood Gym – Time Badge
chunks.x: Benjamin is young. You’ll get TM49 Leech Fang for beating Benjamin, and… he ‘devolved’ too, into a little kid., Nothing less for the bestower of the Time Badge. | The Pokemon League awaits | After You Win | Now there is nothing stopping you from reaching the Pokémon League – except for Victory Road, of course., The trail to Victory Road starts east of Gurun Town, so fly there to get started.

chunks.t: Gym 8: Redwood Village Gym (Benjamin) – Time Badge, Bug
chunks.x: The Redwood Village Gym is the 8th gym you’ll encounter in Pokémon Unbound. The Gym Leader, Benjamin, specializes in Bug-type Pokémon., The Redwood Village Gym features special conditions based on the story of Benjamin Butterfree: when a Pokémon’s HP bar is depleted in battle, it devolves instead of fainting as normal., When a Pokemon reaches its base stage and cannot devolve any further, it faints. Once devolved, Pokemon will be unable to use any moves from their set which require evolution. Mega Evolutions in this Gym do not count as an additional evolution and will be treated as the normal evolved form of a Pokemon. Redwood Gym Puzzle (Step-by-Step): The Redwood Gym features a relatively straightforward puzzle. At the entrance, you’ll find 4 separate rooms, each hosting a rock with a button. The goal here is to figure out the correct sequence in which the buttons must be pressed., Doing this successfully reveals a hidden room leading to the Gym Leader. Here’s how you can solve the puzzle quickly., Step 1: From the entrance, head into the third room from the left (pictured below), A Trainer hides behind this door and will trigger a battle as soon as you enter., Afterward, press the button on the rock directly next to the Trainer and make your way back to the entrance., Step 2: Now, head into the room on the far-left., You’ll have to go through another Trainer battle here., Once that’s done, activate the button on the rock and head back to the entrance., Step 3: Enter the room on the far-right., Complete the Trainer battle in this room., After the fight, press the button situated on the rock and head back outside., Step 4: Lastly, go into the final room you haven’t entered yet (second from the left)., Battle your last Trainer here., Then press the button on the rock and go back to the entrance., Step 5: The hidden room leading to Benjamin will now be revealed. Tips for Defeating Benjamin: Use a Diverse Team: Benjamin is a surprisingly easy Gym Leader with multiple countering strategies and minimal restrictions. However, it’s important to use a well-rounded team that features multiple types of Pokemon so you can effectively counter him., The ideal strategy is to

chunks.x: Camomons Battle House (Optional) | One last training opportunity. You have all eight Badges and are eligible to participate in the Pokémon League – but if you feel your Pokémon team needs a little bit more training, the Camomons Battle House in Seaport City is now open to you. | Six trainers to battle as many times as you wish. However, all battles follow the ‘Camomons’ ruleset., It’s the same ruleset that applied in the Polder Gym: you and your opponent’s Pokémon change their types to the types of the first two moves they know.

First things first:, There’s a Route Master on Route 18, so it’s worth it to find and defeat all the trainers here.

chunks.t: Part 37: Route 18 & Pre-E4 Grind – Route 18
chunks.x: Swimmer Elsie and the first rock. Swimmer Elsie is guarding the first stretch of water, between the shore and the first rocky island you’ll encounter. | Swimmer Darrin is on the east side. Once you’re past the rock, you’ll see Swimmer Darrin, as well as a bit of an opening in the barrier to the north. Surf into it and head west first. | Psychic Preston. There’s a lone trainer on a sand island – this is Psychic Preston., When you defeat him, surf east to the other side of this little pocket.

chunks.t: Part 37: Route 18 & Pre-E4 Grind – Route 18
chunks.x: Black Belt Daisuke, and a Vivillon. You’ll find a Black Belt, and the Marine Vivillon is also here; you can defeat it for the mission (or catch it if you can)., Then head back through the opening into the main route channel and continue east. | Swimmer Spencer. Yet another swimmer is here to block your path – get rid of him and keep on surfing to the east through this long ocean passage. | The next rock, and Swimmer Faye. Eventually you’ll come to another rock, with Swimmer Faye lurking near it. Defeat her and continue on.

chunks.t: Part 37: Route 18 & Pre-E4 Grind – Route 18
chunks.x: Another rock, this time with the Route Master on it. There’s another island to the southeast of Faye that has the Route Master on it – you won’t be able to challenge her until all other trainers on Route 18 are defeated. Make a note of her location though., Surf through the gap just east of her and you’ll see another sand island. | Fisherman Darian’s island. Challenge and defeat Fisherman Darian here, and you can move on back to the main passage. | Keep surfing east. You’ll need to surf across a long stretch of empty water here, but at the end of it is your ultimate destination.

chunks.t: Part 37: Route 18 & Pre-E4 Grind – Route 18
chunks.x: The League is beyond the waterfall. Swimmer Aimee is at the foot of a giant waterfall that serves as the gate to the Pokémon League., But before you climb it, go east and you’ll see one last sand island. | Fisherman Stan and Ninja Boy Hayden. There are two trainers here – Fisherman Stan, out in the open, and Ninja Boy Hayden, who is hiding in a sand mound., Once you’ve taken care of both of them, it’s time to climb that waterfall. | The top of the waterfall

chunks.t: Part 37: Route 18 & Pre-E4 Grind – Route 18
chunks.x: The Victory Road Pokecenter | You’re not quite at Victory Road yet – just a little way further., Jump onto land and head north. | A gift for our journey. There’s a Pokémon Center here that acts as a fast travel point – and it’s probably a valuable sight after beating all those trainers., Tip: Speaking to the man outside the Pokecenter gets you 10 Max Repels, in case you’re sick of wild Pokémon. | A very daunting challenge. The cameraman inside the Pokémon Center gives probably one of, if not the most, challenging missions of the game., Not only do you have to beat the Elite Four with a team made up of just one type of Pokémon, you’ll have to do it eighteen times for each type. | This is something best left until way way later into the endgame, if done at all. But if you manage to do it you will receive a lot of goodies, which include: | 1,000BP for the Battle Frontier, 18 Big Nuggets, And a HeartGold/SoulSilver costume for the Costume Box | Head back outside the Pokémon Center and go north.

chunks.t: Part 37: Route 18 & Pre-E4 Grind – Route 18
chunks.x: There’s a strange Rancher back here. If you talk to the Rancher behind a raised hill just north of the Center, and answer ‘no’ to her question, she’ll give you P1000. This can be repeated every day. | The Gym Badge Checkpoint. Victory Road proper starts at the checkpoint west of the Pokémon Center, where there’s a policeman ready to check your Badges., Once you show him you have all eight, he moves aside and you can begin the ascent. | Ace Trainer Shannon. Keep going north, and you’ll pass by an Ace Trainer Shannon and have to climb some stairs.

chunks.t: Part 37: Route 18 & Pre-E4 Grind – Route 18

The final trainer on the route is Ace Trainer Colby, near the Trainer Tips sign., But with all of the challengers on Route 18 defeated, it’s time to go back to the rock and defeat the Route Master. | Items: Twisted Spoon, Hyper Potion, Focus Sash, Max Revive, Max Repels x10, Big Nugget x18, Red Shard x2, Blue Shard x2, Yellow Shard x2, Green Shard x2, Zygarde Cell #81, Zygarde Cell #82, Zygarde Cell #83, Trainer Tips sign #35, Max Raid Den #19, Vivillon pattern Marine | Special Encounters (Miraheze wiki): Stonjourner (Special), Vivillon (Marine form) Lv50, Azelf (Special encounter) Lv65, Haxorus (Special encounter) Lv59, Rhyperior (Special encounter) Lv60, Dugtrio (Alola form) Lv58

Go back to Victory Road and you’ll see a familiar old man waiting for you at the entrance to the cave system. | The Lucario cult wants us to join. Professor Log wishes you luck and hands over some handy items: | 2 Blue Shards, 2 Red Shards, 2 Yellow Shards, 2 Green Shards | You can use these to trade with move trainers all across Borrius.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 1F
chunks.x: Victory Road – 1F | The first floor of the caverns. The Victory Road caverns are the only obstacle remaining between you and the Pokémon League. It’s a fairly long and dangerous path, but there’s something at the entrance that should help with that. | The Healing Chansey. The Chansey here will heal your Pokémon, you’ll just need to keep coming down to it periodically if the trainers here get a little overwhelming., The way forward to the second floor is currently blocked, so climb the rocks down to the east. | The ladder to the basement. You’ll see a ladder – it leads to the basement floor and a puzzle you need to solve before gaining access to the upper levels.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – B1F
chunks.x: Victory Road – B1F | The basement floor. When you get down the ladder, go south and surf into the pond. | The waterfall leads down to the bottom path. The pond will turn into a waterfall – ride it down and you’ll make it to the lower part of this cavern. | The start of the tiered area. This whole basement floor is a series of tiered balconies with trainers on them – you need to get to the east side of the top section.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – B1F
chunks.x: Climb these rocks first. Walk past the staircase until you see a wall you can climb – go up it and you’ll get challenged by Ace Trainer Paul. | Ace Trainer Paul. Once you’ve beaten him, go east along the ledge and you’ll see another wall to climb – head up it., Then, go west and climb another rock wall to get to the top level and Ace Trainer Brooke. | Ace Trainer Brooke and the top level. After that battle, walk east and you’ll see a one-way ledge for you to jump over. Take it, and continue on east.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – B1F
chunks.x: The Boulder Puzzle | You need this boulder. You’ll see a boulder here, and you need to roll it all the way down three sets of stairs to get to a button., Make sure not to roll it into a position where you can’t get it out again, or you’ll have to reset by changing floors and coming back. | Black Belt Yoshi. Two trainers will challenge you on the way down as well, and Black Belt Yoshi is the first of them., Once he’s out of the way, keep pushing the boulder. | Psychic Gregory. It’s usually better to battle the trainers before they see you with the boulder, because they may mess up your route., Beat Psychic Gregory and push the boulder to the bottom level.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – B1F
chunks.x: The button you need. When you roll the boulder to the button, the ladder to 2F on 1F will now be unblocked. Head back up the waterfall and onto the bridge with the Chansey. | Return to 1F | Super Nerd Avery and the way down to water level. Cross the bridge north and you’ll run into Super Nerd Avery – then head past him and you’ll see a set of stairs leading to the water. | Surf under the bridge. Surf south then east until you go under the bridge. Aim for the northeast shore once you’re on the other side.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Return to 1F
chunks.x: The ladder is now unblocked. Before you pressed the button, there were two rocks here blocking access. Now they’re gone, and you’re free to head to 2F. | Victory Road – 2F | Second floor of the caverns. Once you’re on the second floor, head north across a small pond. | Pokémon Ranger Shanta. You’ll see a trainer on the way past, but you can ignore her if you wish. Head north, climb the stairs and you’ll be in a tunnel.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 2F
chunks.x: The entrance to the maze. At the end of the tunnel is a cave opening to the outside – head on through.

Prize ₽3,600 | Trainer Tuber Elle and Aroma Lady Mya: Wigglytuff (Normal/Fairy) Lv60, Lurantis (Grass) Lv60, Morelull (Grass/Fairy) Lv58, Sunflora (Grass) Lv59. Prize ₽2,120 | Hedge Maze Tutorial | Outside, for a little while. You’re about halfway through Victory Road, and it’s time to take a bit of a break from the caves., You’ll now be in a wooded area – head north. | The hedge maze begins. Unfortunately, you’ll need to make your way through a giant hedge maze here. You can refer to the map above, but we’ll guide you through it step-by-step as well., Take the east path and follow it along until you come to a fork.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Hedge Maze Tutorial
chunks.x: The first fork. Unless you want a Double Battle, take the left path from this fork and continue north for a while. | A bit of long grass to catch Pokemon in. When you get to the walled-in long grass, head east and then north until you find yourself at another junction. | Another junction. From that junction, take the lower of the two paths and go west.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Hedge Maze Tutorial
chunks.x: The final choice to make. You’ll come to a four-way junction – here you should take the southern path, and it will wind all the way around the upper part of the maze until you’re finally free of it. | More caverns await. At the end of the maze is a cave opening, and that will take you to the third floor of the Victory Road caverns.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 3F

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 3F

Prize ₽3,660 | Trainer Pokemon Ranger Chaundra: Magmortar (Fire) Lv61. Prize ₽3,660 | The third floor. When you get inside, go west and you’ll see two Ace Trainers waiting to ambush you with a Double Battle.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 3F
chunks.x: Past the Double Ace Trainers. Defeat them, and continue on west., Climb the stairs and you’ll be on a raised platform. | Take the north stairs. If you’re looking for the shortest route out of here, take the north stairs. | The exit is west. Then, go west until you see Pokémon Ranger Chaundra.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 3F
chunks.x: One more outside section. Once you’ve beaten her, head through the cave opening and you’ll be outside again. It suddenly got a lot colder. | Victory Road – Upper Ascent | Victory Road Upper Ascent map. Ace Trainer Gilbert, Ace Trainer Julie, Kyurem Cave, Polar Vivillon, Mega Trainers Portia and Sterling. (south) Victory Road 3F, (north) Victory Road 4F

Prize ₽4,565 | Trainer Mega Trainers Portia and Sterling: Typhlosion (Fire) Lv60, Meganium (Grass) Lv60, Charizard ((Mega, Y) Fire/Flying) Lv60, Venusaur ((Mega) Grass/Poison) Lv60. Prize ₽12,600 | Emerging into snow. You’re now on the upper snowy slopes of the mountain that holds Victory Road, and you are closer to the Pokémon League.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – Upper Ascent
chunks.x: Ace Trainer Gilbert. Walk west and north up the stairs. Ace Trainer Gilbert is the first to greet you in this new area. | Ace Trainer Julie. Continue north, passing through patches of snowy long grass and climbing stairs until you see Ace Trainer Julie., Past her is a longer staircase that will lead to the upper ledge. | The upper ledge. Once you get there, walk east.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – Upper Ascent
chunks.x: A Mega Trainer Double Battle awaits. Going up north leads to a staircase that goes to the last section of Victory Road, but it’s guarded by a pair of Mega Trainers who will not make beating them easy., Before you take them on, though, climb down the rocks to the south for a little detour. | Kyurem’s Cave. There’s a cave that will be important in the post-game here, though for now it is empty except for some useful Pokémon to catch. | The Polar Vivillon. The Polar Vivillon is to the east of the cave entrance, waiting to be caught or defeated for the mission in Magnolia Town., Once you’ve seen all to see here, go back to the Mega Trainers.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – Upper Ascent
chunks.x: The last trainers on Victory Road. They’re the last trainers you need to defeat before the Pokémon League, and they’ve got a heavy Double Battle team with them. | The last cavern. If you manage to beat them, the only thing left to do is head north into the last cavern along Victory Road.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: Victory Road – 4F | Victory Road 4F map. Teleport Psychic. (south) Victory Road Upper Ascent, (north) Pokémon League | Items: Protector (hidden), Rare Candy (hidden), Ice Stone (hidden), Rockium Z (hidden)

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: Wild Pokémon [Cave]: Golbat (Poison/Flying) Lv56–59 20%, Hariyama (Fighting) Lv56–59 25%, Sealeo (Ice/Water) Lv56–59 30%, Jynx (Ice/Psychic) Lv56–59 10%, Avalugg (Ice), Glalie (Ice) Lv56–59 5%, Piloswine (Ice/Ground) Lv56–59 5% | The final hurdle. That’s right – the last thing before the Pokémon League is an ice puzzle., It’s a particularly challenging one too. | Tip: If you’re really not in the mood to be sliding around trying to find the exit, the Psychic at the entrance will charge you P45,000 to have him teleport you to the entrance of the Pokémon League.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: You can pay your way out of it | The Ice Puzzle | The solution to the ice puzzle

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: If you want to take on the ice puzzle and save some money, you can follow these instructions:, Step 1: Slide north from the left stair tile, to a tall rock. | Start from the left-hand side of the stairs. After the first move | Step 2: Slide west to a rock. | After the second move. Step 3: Slide north to the wall. | After the third move. Step 4: Slide east along the wall to a rock.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: After the fourth move. Step 5: Slide south along the entire length of the ice to a rock. | After the fifth move. Step 6: Slide east to the wall. | After the sixth move. Step 7: Slide south to a rock in the corner.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: After the seventh move. Step 8: Slide west to a rock. | After the eighth move. Step 9: Slide north to a platform on the ice. | After the ninth move. Step 10: Slide east along the length of the ice to a platform on the other side.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: After the tenth move. Step 11: Slide north to another platform. | After the eleventh move. Step 12: Slide west to a rock. | After the twelfth move. Step 13: Slide south to a platform on the ice.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: After the thirteenth move. Step 14: Slide east to a rock. | After the fourteenth move. Step 15: Slide south to a rock. This rock has a hidden Rockium-Z in it, which could be useful to a strong Pokémon that uses Rock-type moves. | After the fifteenth move. Step 16: Slide west to an ice platform.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: After the sixteenth move. Step 17: Slide north to a rock. | After the seventeenth move. Step 18: Slide west to a final rock. | After the eighteenth move. Step 19: Slide north to the exit, at last.

chunks.t: Part 38: Victory Road – Victory Road – 4F
chunks.x: After the nineteenth and final move. You’ve conquered the ice puzzle and are now free to head to the exit of Victory Road. | The exit of Victory Road. Once you pass through that hole in the cavern wall, you’ll be at the Pokémon League. | Exiting Victory Road | The Pokémon League, at last. After eight Gym battles and a journey spanning the length of Borrius, you’re finally here., Time to take that Pokémon Championship crown.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Pokémon League
chunks.x: Pokémon League | The lobby of the Pokemon League. You’ve finally made it to the Borrius Pokémon League!, After defeating the Shadow and the Light of Ruin, beating eight Gyms across Borrius and making a name for yourself, you’re finally here to challenge for the vacant Championship. | To succeed, you must beat all five trainers without returning to the lobby. Make sure you’re stocked up on Revives and Full Restores. | Tip: If you’re up for a challenge, take the Youngster up on his mission and try and become Champion with just one Pokémon in your team. This almost-impossible feat will be rewarded with an Ultranecrozium-Z.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Pokémon League
chunks.x: One more impossible mission. The League awaits | Speak to the man guarding the door to get started., The Elite Four can be defeated in any order, but for simplicity’s sake it’s probably best to go left to right., Once you’ve beaten all of them, the way to the Champion will open., Even on the easiest difficulty, the trainers in the Pokémon League are all scaled to match the level of your team, so there’s no point in grinding – you’ve got to have strong moves and strong type matchups to succeed. | Moleman’s entrance. The first door on the left leads to Moleman, the Ground trainer. | Items: Ultranecrozium Z, Trainer Tips sign #36, Zygarde Cell #88

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Pokémon League
chunks.x: Special Encounters (Miraheze wiki): Latias (Special) Lv40, Latios (Special) Lv40 | Elite Four – Moleman (Ground) | The Mole-Man is ready to destroy you. Moleman has a team of all Ground-types. Ground-type moves are super-effective against Electric-, Fire-, Poison-, Rock-, and Steel-type Pokémon., They’re weak to Grass-, Ice-, and Water-type moves. | Trainer Elite Four Moleman (Double Battle): Excadrill (Ground/Steel) Lvscales, Flygon (Ground/Dragon) Lvscales, Gliscor (Ground/Flying) Lvscales, Quagsire (Water/Ground) Lvscales. Prize ₽15,200 | This is the first Double Battle in the Pokémon League, so make sure you have two Pokémon that can withstand Moleman’s attacks., Alolan Ninetales with that Icium-Z may come in handy, though not for Excadrill. Be flexible with type matchups and make sure you’re not caught out by strong moves like Earthquake.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Elite Four – Moleman (Ground)
chunks.x: One down, three to go. With Moleman defeated, head back to the hallway., Go to the next door, just left of the statues in the middle, to challenge Elias. | Elite Four – Elias (Ghost) | Elias is a zombie trainer. Apparently the trainer shortage in the Pokémon League is so bad they revived a dead member and turned him into a zombie. This is Elias, the Ghost-type trainer., Ghost-type moves are super-effective against Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokémon, and Ghost-type Pokémon are weak against Ghost- and Dark-type moves. | Trainer Elite Four Elias: Mimikyu (Ghost/Fairy) Lvscales, Aegislash (Steel/Ghost) Lvscales, Chandelure (Ghost/Fire) Lvscales, Banette ((Mega) Ghost) Lvscales. Prize ₽15,200 | It’s a singles battle, so it may be slightly easier than Moleman. Ghost-types tend to have multiple tricky moves up their sleeve, though, and Elias’ team is no exception.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Elite Four – Elias (Ghost)
chunks.x: Half of the Elite Four down. With Elias out of the way, there are just two Elite Four between you and the Championship., Head outside and to the door to the right – time to face Arabella. | Elite Four – Arabella (Fairy) | Arabella is a Fairy-type Pokémon Princess. Arabella may be young but she’s no pushover. She has a team of Fairy-types, and they’re stronger than they may look., Fairy-type moves are super-effective against Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-type Pokémon. However, Fairy-type Pokémon are weak against Poison- and Steel-type moves. | Trainer Elite Four Arabella: Ribombee (Bug/Fairy) Lvscales, Sylveon (Fairy) Lvscales, Azumarill (Water/Fairy) Lvscales, Mawile ((Mega) Steel/Fairy) Lvscales. Prize ₽15,200 | The Mega Mawile may pose a problem if you’re using Steel-type moves against Arabella’s team, though that’s nothing a strong Fire-type move won’t fix.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Elite Four – Arabella (Fairy)
chunks.x: Apparently her father used to be her predecessor. When you defeat Arabella, you’ll be three-quarters done with the Elite Four and free to move on to the final door., Go to the final door on the right and get ready to face Penny. | Elite Four – Penny (Dragon) | The Dragon trainer Penny. Penny loves Dragon-type Pokémon, and has a team full of them., Dragon-types are weak against Dragon-, Fairy-, and Ice-type moves. However, Dragon-type moves are super-effective against Dragon-type Pokémon. | Trainer Elite Four Penny (Double Battle): Goodra (Dragon) Lvscales, Tyrantrum (Rock/Dragon) Lvscales, Kommo-o (Dragon/Fighting) Lvscales, Sceptile ((Mega) Grass/Dragon) Lvscales. Prize ₽15,200 | It’s a Double Battle against Penny, so prepare accordingly., Compared to the other three trainers in the Elite Four, you may have an easier time of it.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Elite Four – Penny (Dragon)
chunks.x: The Elite Four are vanquished. With all of the Elite Four defeated, head back to the hallway and you’ll see a path has opened up. | The way to the Hall of Fame. The corridor between the statues is now visible – take it, and walk right into the empty Championship. | Final Battle – Jax | Jax is here to fight you for the Championship.. Well, it’s not really that empty, it turns out., Jax has already beaten the Elite Four and is ready to challenge you for the open Championship title.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Final Battle – Jax
chunks.x: You and Jax, at the end. It’s a Double Battle, with enough variety in the team to keep it very interesting. Make sure your team has enough PP for their powerful moves. | Trainer Challenger Jax (Double Battle): Golurk (Ground/Ghost) Lvscales, Staraptor (Normal/Flying) Lvscales, Magnezone (Electric/Steel) Lvscales, Pyroar (Fire/Normal) Lvscales, Gastrodon (Water/Ground) Lvscales, Salamence ((Mega) Dragon/Flying) Lvscales. Prize ₽18,000 | Jax proclaims you the new Champion. Once you beat him, Jax recognizes your strength and takes you to the Hall of Fame to enter you in history.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Final Battle – Jax
chunks.x: Submit your Pokemon to the Hall of Fame. You’re now the new Borrius Pokémon League Champion! | After You Win | The end, but not quite. The credits roll – for the first time., Pokémon Unbound is not over yet – it has an endgame much larger than a lot of other Pokémon ROMhacks out there, and as soon as the credits finish you’re taken straight to it. | Beginning the Post-Game | You’re back at Frozen Heights. You’ll find yourself back at Frozen Heights, in front of your house.

chunks.t: Part 39: The Pokémon League – Beginning the Post-Game
chunks.x: Marlon and your Rival show up. You’ll be met by two familiar faces, Marlon and your Rival, who tell you about the now-open Battle Frontier and encourage you to explore. | Professor Log also shows up. Professor Log is pleased as punch that he finally got one over his rival Arthur, but he doesn’t have much time to celebrate., Apparently Hoopa going mad at Crystal Peak has had some side-effects, and there are 25 strange Pokémon you need to defeat across Borrius to close their portals. | Then go inside your house, and you’ll find a letter that’s got to be the biggest post-game hook there is. | Uh oh. It seems like Aklove is not done with you yet.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – The Advanced Digging and Diving Machine
chunks.x: The Advanced Digging and Diving Machine | Aklove’s letter. When you become Champion of the Pokémon League, your journey isn’t over yet., Aklove kidnaps your mother and takes her to an area of the Ruins of Void you previously couldn’t get to – the depths, whose entrance is underwater. | To go underwater, you’ll need the ADM – the Advanced Digging and Diving Machine – and HM05 Dive.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – The Advanced Digging and Diving Machine
chunks.x: The Seaport City Shipyard. There’s only one place you can get the ADM, and that’s the Shipyard in Seaport City., It’s just east of the KBT Expressway entrance, in the northeast part of town (pictured above). | A hefty price. Captain Davy previously told you that he only sells these things to important people – and since you’re Pokémon Champion, you can’t get much more important than that., But that doesn’t stop him from charging you a lot of money for it. P250,000 is his price. | The ADM is worth the money though, because it not only enables you to explore new areas, but also adds convenience to using HMs. | The ultimate in HM tech. To use a HM like Cut or Rock Smash, you would normally have to have at least one Pokémon in your party capable of using the move. With the ADM, that’s no longer necessary., You can now use Dive in areas with deep water, and Dig in underground or underwater tunnels. | With that key piece of equipment acquired, fly to the Ruins of Void.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Exterior (Submerged Access)
chunks.x: Ruins of Void – Exterior (Submerged Access) | Ruins of Void exterior map (partial). Ruins of Void B3F, Ruins of Void B2F, Ruins of Void Submerged Floor (South), Ruins of Void Submerged Floor (Southeast), Ruins of Void Submerged Floor (East), Ruins of Void B1F Claydol Maze | Items: TM48 Skill Swap

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Exterior (Submerged Access)
chunks.x: Wild Pokémon [Surfing]: Tentacool (Water/Poison) Lv35–40 60%, Tentacruel (Water/Poison) Lv38–40 5%, Pelipper (Water/Flying) Lv35–40 30%, Mantine (Water/Flying) Lv37–40 5%, Golduck (Water) | Wild Pokémon [Fishing]: Magikarp (Water (Old Rod)) Lv10–15 100%, Horsea (Water (Good Rod)) Lv20–25 60%, Shellder (Water (Good Rod)) Lv20–50, Shellder (Water (Super Rod)) Lv20–50, Gyarados (Water/Flying (Super Rod)) Lv45–50 19%, Seadra (Water (Super Rod)) Lv45–50 40%, Kingdra (Water/Dragon (Super Rod)) Lv45–50 1% | Arriving at the Ruins. When you arrive on the landing platform, climb the rocks to the left of the cave entrance. They’ll take you to the first ledge level.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Exterior (Submerged Access)
chunks.x: The path to the Dive area. Go west along the ledge until you see another spot for you to climb the rocks down. | A deep patch of water. You’ll be back down at water level, and you’ll see an A-shaped deep patch of water just to the west of you. | Using the ADM. Surf over to the deep patch and press A – you’ll be prompted to dive beneath the waves.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Submerged Floor
chunks.x: Ruins of Void – Submerged Floor | Ruins of Void submerged floor map. Dynamax Toxapex (Post-Aklove), Ancient Tablet. Ruins of Void Exterior (South), Ruins of Void Exterior (Southeast), Ruins of Void Exterior (East)

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Submerged Floor
chunks.x: Items: Red Shard (hidden), Sea Salt, Blue Shard (hidden), Yellow Shard (hidden), Green Shard (hidden), Sea Shell | Items: Green Shard (hidden)

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Submerged Floor
chunks.x: Wild Pokémon [Underwater]: Clamperl (Water) Lv35–50 50%, Mareanie (Poison/Water) Lv35–50 20%, Toxapex (Poison/Water) Lv40–60 10%, Chinchou (Water/Electric) Lv35–50 10%, Lanturn (Water/Flying) Lv40–60 4%, Luvdisc (Water) Lv35–60 5%, Relicanth (Water/Rock) Lv40–60 1% | The ADM submarine. It seems the ADM transforms itself into a red mini sub!, In this underwater section, as with the others in Routes 14, 16, and 17, you’ll see collapsed cave entrances. If you interact with them, you’ll be prompted to Dig and will be treated to a version of the Crater Town KBT Expressway digging minigame. | For now, pilot the sub east. | Pass by a cavern entrance. You will soon pass an opening to the north. This leads to the lair of a Dynamax Toxapex, but it won’t be there until you defeat Aklove., Keep going east, through a narrow gap.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Submerged Floor
chunks.x: Another ascension point. The patch of sunlight on the seafloor indicates a place where you can resurface – it’ll lead to another closed-off part of the Ruins of Void exterior and will have a TM for you to collect., Ignore or explore if you like, and if you want to move on, go north through another narrow passage. | The narrow passage. Keep going through the narrow passage, and it will soon widen. | The final ascension point. When the passage gets wider, you’ll see another point where you can ascend to the surface., The way north leads to an ancient tablet, solved by the Toxapex you can defeat later on.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Submerged Floor
chunks.x: Surface to the Ruins again. Press B in the middle of the patch of sunlight and you’ll return to the surface. | The entrance to the Claydol Maze. When you resurface, you’ll be right next to the entrance to a new part of the ruins., Head on inside.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze | Claydol Maze map. Dusclops Maze Gate, First Gate Switch, Second Gate Switch, Third Gate Switch, Fourth Gate Switch. Ruins of Void Exterior, Ruins of Void Aklove’s Chamber | Items: Nugget

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: Wild Pokémon [Ruins]: Claydol (Ground/Psychic) Lv60–65 30%, Cofagrigus (Ghost) Lv34–65, Dusclops (Ghost) Lv34–65, Sableye (Dark/Ghost) Lv34–65 10%, Bronzong (Dark/Steel) Lv34–65 5%, Lunatone (Rock/Psychic) Lv34–65 4%, Solrock (Rock/Psychic) Lv34–65 4%, Sigilyph (Psychic/Flying) Lv34–65 1% | This area is similar to the maze filled with Dusclops earlier, and it resembles the stealth puzzles in the Crater Gym and the Ferrothorn Turf. | Entering the Maze. The maze is filled with moving Claydol. If they spot you, they’ll teleport you back to a checkpoint and you’ll need to try that section again. | The first gate, with its switch next to it. There are five switches in the maze – four are required to be activated to move forward to the end., The odd one out is the switch in the far southeast, which will open up a section that was previously blocked off on B3F, with all the Dusclops.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: Ignore that for now and walk west from the entrance. You’ll see the first gate and the first Claydol to avoid. The switch is in the passage just to the left of the gate., Once that first gate is open, head north and you’ll see another patrolling Claydol. | The second Claydol. Go right at the junction. | The second switch. Pull the second switch here, then return to the junction, hopefully avoiding the Claydol along the way., The way will be clear to continue west and then south along the passage. | Past the second Claydol. There’s a third Claydol patrolling here, so use the gap in the eastern wall to hide when you can.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: The third Claydol and the intersection. There will be an intersection next, with a path to the west and a path to the south., Go south first. | The third switch. It’ll lead to a third switch, which you’ll need to activate to proceed., With that done, go back to the intersection. | Taking the west passage. Avoid the Claydol again and go west from here.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: The fourth sentry. The path will snake around, with a fourth Claydol here to keep you on your toes., This one is a little tricky to get past – you’ll have to time it exactly so you can slip past at the top corner just as the Claydol changes direction. | More gaps in the wall. Once you’re through that, there’s yet another Claydol sentry you will need to slip past. There are two gaps in the wall along this passage that should allow you to do it. | The second gap in the hallway and the fifth Claydol. When you get through that section, you’ve only got two switches left to pull.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: A bigger gap. Head west and you’ll see another intersection, past a large wall gap. | The fourth switch and the sixth Claydol. The switch that opens the way forward is in the west passage, and after activating it you’ll be free to go north., Just be aware that the sixth and final Claydol here has a long patrol path. | The final gate. There’s only one more switch to go, and it’s at the end of the tunnel that points northeast.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: The final switch. Flip it, then head back to the area with the ladder. | Dynamax Claydol Battle | One last obstacle. There’s another Claydol here, but it’s not a mere sentry. This one you’ll need to fight, and in a Dynamax Battle too. | Trainer Dynamax Battle: Claydol (Ground/Psychic (level scaled)) Lv?

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Ruins of Void – Claydol Maze
chunks.x: The way up is clear. If you manage to defeat it, there’s now nothing between you and Aklove but a ladder. | Final Showdown with Aklove | You’ll see that Aklove has captured not only your mother, but also Jax’s grandfather Arthur and the son of Zeph. | Aklove has captured a lot of loved ones. There’s a healing Chansey in the eastern part of the room if you want a bit of a refresh. | A final double battle. When you go to confront Aklove, Jax rushes in and you’re asked to pick three Pokémon to use in a Double Battle alongside Jax’ Staraptor, Magnezone, and Golurk.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Final Showdown with Aklove
chunks.x: Trainer Aklove Final Showdown (Double Battle): Klefki (Steel/Fairy) Lv70, Roserade (Grass/Poison) Lv72, Togekiss (Fairy/Flying) Lv72, Raichu (Electric) Lv73, Primarina (Water/Fairy) Lv74, Gardevoir ((Mega) Psychic/Fairy) Lv74 | After You Win | Marlon comes with the cops. After defeating Aklove for the final time, Marlon arrives with the police to throw him in jail for good. | Finally, the main story quest is over. And with that, this small section of the post-game story is complete., Your Mom advises you to rest, and the credits roll for a second time.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Final Showdown with Aklove
chunks.x: The second credit roll. The credits are unskippable, but worth watching again. | Completing this unlocks a few things. After defeating Aklove, you’ll now have access to New Game+, which comes with its own set of rules., In addition, your Mission Log got a very welcome addition to it. | The locations of remaining missions. Now, Missions you have not yet obtained show up as question marks in the log, with the location and face of the mission starters displayed., This will be helpful in mopping up all the post-game missions that have emerged after defeating the Pokémon League. | And that’s not all – once you’ve seen the credits and explored the new features, go back to the chamber where you beat Aklove to pick up that item that was next to him – a Primarium Z.

chunks.t: Part 40: Post-Game Ruins of Void & Saving Mom – Final Showdown with Aklove
chunks.x: The last reward. So with that, the main story of Pokémon Unbound finally comes to an end.
